claims.evidence: YTM1173 = the SILAC strain named in Yeast strains ("For SILAC, a modified BY4741 strain was used (YTM1173: ...)"). exp1 heat-shock supernatant rep1-4 = MaxQuant experiments MSZ20_S_1..4; LiP names encode the PK:lysate w/w dilution from the file tag. "pre-existing-proteome" (light), "newly-synthesized-proteome" (heavy pulse) and "medium-SILAC_reference-lysate" are the channel roles stated in Methods and the Fig. 7 legend. Medium reference rows carry one source name per run (aliquot mixed into that run) because one reference extract was mixed into all 7 LiP runs.

claims.value: MATa his3delta1 leu2delta0 ura3delta0 MET15 arg4delta::KanMX6 lys2delta0
claims.evidence: Yeast strains: "For SILAC, a modified BY4741 strain was used (YTM1173: MATa, his3Δ1, leu2Δ0, ura3Δ0, MET15, arg4Δ::KanMX6, lys2Δ0)". Δ written as "delta" (ASCII), as in curated yeast SDRF PXD000554. Applies to all SILAC experiments (Exp1 and LiP).

claims.location: characteristics[organism part] / characteristics[cell type] / characteristics[disease] rows 1-29
claims.evidence: Unicellular yeast culture: no anatomical part, no CL cell type, no disease; same encoding as curated yeast SDRFs.
Cultured yeast cells lysed by cryo-grinding; curated yeast SDRFs use "cell".

Results: Experiment 1 "We quantified 3,410 proteins in four biological replicates"; the supernatant search has four MaxQuant experiments MSZ20_S_1..4 (one file each, ~1,180-1,220 protein groups each, pairwise intensity r 0.92-0.94 -> replicates, not high-pH fractions). Light and heavy rows of one file come from the same culture and share its number (rule 3).
LiP Methods describe one pulsed culture (lysate split across PK amounts) and one separate medium-labelled culture; within the "untreated" factor group the two cultures get different numbers (rule 3).

Exp1: after 15 min in heavy medium at 25°C cells were heat shocked "for 20 minutes at 45°C". No NCIT/EFO term for a heat-shock treatment exists (OLS: NCIT:C17888/EFO:0022044 are the response process, EFO:0001762 a design type, NCIT:C15415 therapeutic hyperthermia), so free text; validator warning accepted.

claims.value: proteinase K treatment (PK runs, light+heavy) / untreated (Ref light+heavy, all medium rows)
claims.evidence: LiP Methods: lysates received 0, 0.01, 0.05, 0.2, 1, 5, 20 ng PK per µg lysate for 5 min at 20°C; "No PK was added to medium SILAC labeled cells". Controls written "untreated" (rule 4). LiP cells were not heat shocked (Discussion: "in the LiP experiment (in which no heat shock was performed)").
PK = SIGMA P2308; CHEBI:201492 "Proteinase K". not applicable on untreated rows and Exp1 rows.

File tag = PK:lysate dilution: Results "the sample treated with a 1:1,000 protease dilution (1 ng of PK per microgram of sample)" -> 1k = 1 ng/µg; hence 50=1:50=20 ng/µg, 200=5, 5k=0.2, 20k=0.05, 100k=0.01 ng/µg, matching the 7 amounts in Methods (0 = Ref). Written as mass ratio in mg/kg (1 ng/µg = 1 mg/g = 1000 mg/kg) because ng/ug is not an allowed unit. Data check: summed light/medium intensity in peptides.txt falls only at the highest PK amounts (50: 0.49, 200: 0.84, 1k-100k/Ref: 0.96-1.02), as expected if 50 is the largest dose.

claims.location: characteristics[exposure duration] rows 1-8 and PK rows of rows 9-29 (MSZ23_LiP_*)
claims.evidence: Exp1 heat shock 20 min at 45°C; LiP PK incubation 5 min at 20°C; not applicable on untreated rows.

Exp1: grown in light Lys0/Arg0, pulsed in heavy D4 Lys-4 + 13C6 Arg-6 for 15 min + 20 min heat shock; MaxQuant has a 2-plex L/H design. Data check: median H/L 0.089-0.102 per replicate = small newly-synthesised fraction, consistent with H = pulse (paper: median H/L ~11% in TCL).

claims.value: SILAC light / SILAC medium / SILAC heavy
claims.evidence: LiP Methods + Fig. 7A: light = pre-existing proteome of the pulsed culture, heavy = 15-min pulse (Lys-8/Arg-10) in the same culture, medium = separately grown Lys4/Arg6 reference without PK, mixed 1:1. Data check (peptides.txt): Ref M/L median 0.98 (1:1 mix), H/L 0.23 median / summed H/L 0.09 (small pulse); L/M falls with PK amount while M is untreated.

claims.location: comment[modification parameters] (Label:13C(6)15N(4) R UNIMOD:267, Label:13C(6)15N(2) K UNIMOD:259) rows 9-29 (MSZ23_LiP_*); not applicable rows 1-8 (MSZ20_Sup_1..4)
claims.evidence: LiP heavy = "Lys-8" and "Arg-10" (the LiP paragraph prefixes them "D4"/"13C6", a copy error: D4-Lys is +4 and 13C6-Arg is +6, identical to the medium channel, which MaxQuant could not have separated; the Exp3 paragraph of the same Methods gives "13C6 15N2 Lys-8 and 13C6 15N4 Arg-10"). Nominal +8/+10 -> UNIMOD:259/267. The LiP search is 3-plex (Ratio M/L, H/L, H/M columns). The Exp1 search is 2-plex L/H, so those two columns are not applicable on rows 1-8 (rule 5).
.baf headers contain "impact 2" and "Bruker otofControl"; Methods "Impact II (Bruker)"; PRIDE instruments "impact II".
Impact II is a quadrupole time-of-flight instrument (Beck 2015 title); MS/MS read out in the TOF.

QTOF collision-cell CID with collision energy 23-65 eV (Methods). Beam-type CID = CID in a beam-type collision cell (MS:1000422 definition); inferred from the instrument geometry, not named in the paper.
"data-dependent auto-MS/MS mode ... fragmenting the 20 most abundant ions".

Methods: "trypsin digested using ... SP3"; search: "trypsin enzyme specificity". Rule 2: digestion enzyme. reconcile flags MINOR cleavage_agent_unsupported because the PRIDE record text is not parsed for the digest; refuted in validation.txt.
"full-range scan from m/z 200 Th to m/z 2000 Th".

INFERRED, as above: Beck 2015 "The allowed fragment mass deviation was 40 ppm" (MaxQuant TOF default).

limitations: Precursor (0.07 Da) and fragment (40 ppm) tolerances are inferred from MaxQuant QTOF defaults as published in Beck et al. 2015; no mqpar.xml/parameters.txt was deposited.

The heavy LiP label (Lys8/Arg10 -> UNIMOD:259/267) rests on the nominal masses "Lys-8"/"Arg-10"; the LiP paragraph prefixes them "D4"/"13C6", which is internally inconsistent. No deposited table carries label masses (no evidence.txt/mqpar).

Mapping of LiP file tags (50 ... 100k) to PK amounts rests on the paper equating "1:1,000 protease dilution" with "1 ng of PK per microgram"; PRIDE protocol omits the 0.01 ng/µg amount that file 100k represents (paper lists it).
MSZ20_Sup_1..4 = biological replicates 1-4 is inferred from "four biological replicates" for Experiment 1 plus four separate MaxQuant experiments; no file-to-replicate table exists.
Heat shock, proteinase K treatment and untreated have no NCIT/EFO term; free text gives three validator warnings.
Dose written as mg/kg (1 ng/µg = 1000 mg/kg) to stay inside the allowed unit list; the source unit is ng PK per µg lysate.

Pulse duration (15 min heavy before heat shock in Exp1; 15 min heavy in LiP), the heat-shock temperature (45°C), culture medium (SD + 2% dextrose) and the LC system (EASY-nLC 1000 or nanoElute, per-run unknown) have no licensed column and are recorded only in the report.

Strain name (BY4741-derived YTM1173) has no licensed column without an organism template (characteristics[strain or breed] is licensed by vertebrates/invertebrates/plants only); it is in the source names and genotype.
The LiP MaxQuant search also contains an experiment "ref_3hr" with no deposited raw file; it is not annotated.
Collision energy (23-65 eV, stepped by m/z and charge) is not a single value and is omitted.
